subject.title: Browser tool: 7 improvements from real-world automation field test

question: Which remaining browser automation slice should OpenClaw own next: model-facing batch/sequence exposure, page readiness and stale-ref signals, CDP inspectElement, CAPTCHA signaling, or fill verification?
rationale: Current main already shipped some high-impact pieces, but the unresolved pieces change browser tool API shape and agent behavior, so automation should not choose the product surface from this umbrella report alone.

options.title: Slice readiness and staleness first
options.body: Define a compact snapshot/action signal for empty hydration, stale refs, and blockers, then require a focused live repro before coding.

options.title: Expose model-facing batch first
options.body: Promote the existing lower-level batch support into the Browser tool schema and docs with compatibility tests for provider schemas.

options.title: Split into separate design issues
options.body: Keep this umbrella open only as context and create narrower maintainer-owned issues for each remaining browser API surface.

recommendation.title: Slice readiness and staleness first
recommendation.body: Define a compact snapshot/action signal for empty hydration, stale refs, and blockers, then require a focused live repro before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored the merged selector/batch browser PR and has the clearest recent history on the partially implemented surface.
